newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae to cut costs, originate loans -- new CEO.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae to cut costs, originate loans -- new CEO.

text.p: The incoming management of the Student Loan Marketing Association plans to make its first priority the reduction of loan acquisition costs, but it also plans to originate student loans.
"The objective is to acquire as many student loans at the best price possible," incoming chief executive Albert Lord told reporters Thursday.

"I do think we'll be originating at least as many loans as we have planned," he added, referring to already-set loan level targets for the future. Sallie Mae, currently undergoing a transition, has not originated loans in the past.
Lord said Sallie Mae hoped to cut acquisition costs in half. The company currently pays a margin of about two percent on cash purchases of loans, he said.
Loan origination would give Sallie Mae an alternative to relying solely on the banks that currently fund student loans, he said.
Asked where funds to issue loans would come from, Lord said Sallie Mae would use the same resources it currently uses to fund loan acquisitions.
"The funding mechanism will remain the same," Lord said.
At a special shareholder meeting on Thursday, stock owners voted in support of a restructuring and privatization plan proposed by the dissident Committee to Restore Value.
By a vote of about 25.5 million to 18.5 million, shareholders approved the board of directors nominated by the CRV, a CRV spokesperson said.
The newly elected board may take charge as early as next week, after an official vote tally is announced, said incoming chairman Edward Fox.
"There will be a certified count, possibly as early as Tuesday afternoon. As soon as we have a sense of the certification, the board will convene," Fox said.

Sallie Mae's business currently consists of purchasing student loans, keeping some in its portfolio and securitizing others for sale to investors. The new CRV management plans to diversify not only into loan origination but also into unrelated areas such as software development.
